articles.title: After NEET-UG paper leak, NTA floats Rs 7.5 crore tender to strengthen exam security
articles.description: NTA Exam Security: Following the NEET-UG 2026 leak, NTA issues a Rs 7.5 crore tender to bolster headquarters' security. The contract ensures 24x7 protection, focuses on safeguarding examination records, and demands strict agency criteria and crowd control.

articles.title: After Neet controversy, NTA moves to tighten security with ₹7.5 cr tender
articles.description: Following the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak controversy, the National Testing Agency (NTA) has floated a Rs 7.5-crore tender for round-the-clock security services at its headquarters at Minto Road, regional offices at Okhla, storage facilities and other notified locations. According to the tender document, the move aims to safeguard NTA's personnel, visitors, assets, premises, records, confidential examination material, server rooms, strong rooms and other critical infrastructure. The July 25 Request for Proposal (RFP) said the estimated contract value is "Rs 7.5 crore plus GST (tentative) for a 2-year contract without variation". Bids can be submitted until 3 pm on August 17, and the printing-services tender closes on August 20, it said. The contract will initially remain valid for two years and can be extended for two additional one-year periods, subject to satisfactory performance, mutual consent and approval of the competent authority. articles.title: NTA floats Rs 7.5 cr security tender to tighten exam safeguards after NEET paper leak
articles.description: The National Testing Agency is enhancing its security infrastructure with a tender valued at Rs 7.5 crore. This initiative aims to strengthen safeguards across its examination processes and facilities. The agency seeks a security firm to manage its headquarters and regional offices. Bids are being accepted until August 17 for this crucial security contract. This move follows the recent NEET paper leak controversy and aims to rebuild public trust.
